DOCUMENT:
Vendor Comparison: Standard Parcel Delivery Contract
Larkspur Home, Operations, June 2026

1. Purpose
Our contract with our current standard-delivery carrier ends on 30 September 2026. This paper compares three shortlisted carriers and recommends which should carry our standard (two-to-four-day) parcels from October.

2. Volumes and requirements
We dispatch an average of 42,000 standard parcels a month: about 70% weigh under 2 kg (cushions, textiles, small homeware) and 30% weigh 2 to 10 kg (lamps, mirrors, small furniture). Our requirements are on-time delivery of at least 95%, a damage rate below 0.5%, full tracking, and a returns service.

Damage and loss matter to us commercially. Each damaged or lost parcel costs us on average £48 in replacement stock, return shipping and customer service time, and damaged items are the most common cause of one-star reviews.

3. Trial
Between 1 April and 31 May 2026, each shortlisted carrier delivered a share of our orders, allocated at random by the warehouse management system, about 5,000 parcels per carrier. We measured on-time delivery against the promised date, damage reported by customers within 14 days, and lost parcels.

Table 1. Prices and trial performance
Carrier | Price, under 2 kg | Price, 2-10 kg | On-time delivery | Damage rate | Lost per 10,000 parcels
SwiftDrop | £3.10 | £4.60 | 96.2% | 0.4% | 3
ParcelLine | £2.85 | £4.95 | 93.1% | 0.9% | 8
Meridian | £3.30 | £4.40 | 97.5% | 0.3% | 2

On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial, and all three offer full tracking and a returns service.

4. Cost comparison
Applying our 70/30 weight mix, the average cost per parcel is £3.55 for SwiftDrop, £3.48 for ParcelLine and £3.63 for Meridian. On 42,000 parcels a month, the monthly cost would be £149,100 for SwiftDrop, £146,160 for ParcelLine and £152,460 for Meridian. ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop and £6,300 a month against Meridian, or between about £35,000 and £76,000 a year.

5. Customer contact
"Where is my order?" contacts are our largest single category of customer service enquiry. During the trial, ParcelLine deliveries generated 6 such contacts per 1,000 parcels, compared with 11 for SwiftDrop and 10 for Meridian. ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts, and at an average handling cost of £3.20 per contact this would save about £670 a month at our volumes. From 1 May, ParcelLine parcels also carried our new proactive delivery-day text message, which we were testing on one carrier before rolling it out.

6. Other considerations
All three carriers can collect from our warehouse daily at 6 pm. ParcelLine and SwiftDrop offer a 12-month contract; Meridian requires 24 months. SwiftDrop and Meridian have both handled our peak-season volumes for other retailers of similar size, while ParcelLine's references were mainly from fashion retailers with lighter parcels.

All three carriers integrate with our warehouse management system through standard interfaces, and none would require changes to our packing process or labelling. Each offers recipients a delivery-preference service to nominate a safe place or a neighbour, and each provides proof-of-delivery photographs, which our customer service team has found useful in resolving disputes.

7. Recommendation
ParcelLine offers the lowest delivery cost, met our service requirements in the trial and reduces customer contacts through its tracking app. We recommend awarding the standard parcel contract to ParcelLine for 12 months from 1 October 2026, saving up to £76,000 a year against the alternatives.

KEY (three known flaws):
1. [misread_evidence] at: "On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial" -- Table 1 shows ParcelLine's on-time delivery was 93.1%, below the 95% requirement. The claim (and the recommendation that ParcelLine 'met our service requirements') misreads the table; ParcelLine's 0.9% damage rate also fails the stated 0.5% requirement.
2. [unsupported_causal] at: "ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts" -- The document states that from 1 May ParcelLine parcels alone also carried the new proactive delivery-day text message. That concurrent intervention confounds the comparison, so the lower contact rate cannot be attributed to ParcelLine's tracking app.
3. [missing_consideration] at: "ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop" -- The cost comparison ignores the stated £48 cost of each damaged or lost parcel. ParcelLine's damage and loss rates (0.9% and 8 per 10,000) versus SwiftDrop's (0.4% and 3 per 10,000) imply about 231 extra problem parcels a month (about £11,100), far exceeding the £2,940 price saving; ParcelLine is likely the most expensive option overall.

REVIEW:
# Review: Vendor Comparison, Standard Parcel Delivery Contract (Larkspur Home)

## What the paper claims

The paper recommends ParcelLine for 12 months. It argues that ParcelLine is cheapest on the 70/30 weight mix, saving about £35,000–£76,000 a year; that all three carriers met the 95% on-time requirement in a randomised trial; and that ParcelLine's tracking app halved "where is my order?" contacts.

## Verdict

The trial design is good, and the price arithmetic is correct. But the recommendation is contradicted by the paper's own Table 1:

- **ParcelLine fails two of the four stated requirements.** It was 93.1% on time against a 95% minimum, and had a 0.9% damage rate against a 0.5% maximum.
- **ParcelLine is the most expensive option overall.** Once damage and loss are costed at the paper's own £48 per parcel, it costs about £90,000 a year more than SwiftDrop.
- **The reduction in contacts can't be credited to the app.** ParcelLine parcels also carried the new delivery-day text from 1 May.

On these figures, SwiftDrop is the stronger recommendation.

## Arithmetic

| Item | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Average cost per parcel | 70/30 weight mix | £3.55 / £3.48 / £3.63 ✓ |
| Monthly delivery cost | × 42,000 parcels | £149,100 / £146,160 / £152,460 ✓ |
| ParcelLine's monthly saving | Against SwiftDrop / Meridian | £2,940 / £6,300 ✓ |
| ParcelLine's annual saving | Against SwiftDrop / Meridian | £35,280 / £75,600 ✓ |
| Contact saving | (11 − 6) per 1,000 × 42,000 × £3.20 | £672 a month ✓ |

The arithmetic is correct. The problems are in what it leaves out and in how the trial results are read.

## 1. ParcelLine did not meet the service requirements

| Requirement | SwiftDrop | ParcelLine | Meridian |
|---|---|---|---|
| On time ≥ 95% | 96.2% ✓ | **93.1% ✗** | 97.5% ✓ |
| Damage < 0.5% | 0.4% ✓ | **0.9% ✗** | 0.3% ✓ |
| Full tracking | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Returns service | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

§3 states that "on-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers," and the author's note repeats it. Table 1 shows ParcelLine at 93.1%. Its damage rate is almost twice the maximum, and the paper doesn't mention this anywhere.

These gaps are not trial noise. With about 5,000 parcels per carrier, 93.1% on time sits well below 95%, and 0.9% damage means about 45 damaged parcels, against about 20 for SwiftDrop. The lost-parcel figures rest on very few events (a handful per carrier), so treat those as indicative only.

## 2. All-in cost reverses the ranking

§2 puts the cost of each damaged or lost parcel at £48. Applying that, and the contact handling cost from §5, at 42,000 parcels a month:

| Monthly cost | SwiftDrop | ParcelLine | Meridian |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delivery | £149,100 | £146,160 | £152,460 |
| Damage and loss (rate × 42,000 × £48) | £8,670 (0.43%) | £19,760 (0.98%) | £6,450 (0.32%) |
| "Where is my order?" contacts (× £3.20) | £1,480 | £810 | £1,340 |
| **Total** | **£159,250** | **£166,720** | **£160,260** |

On this basis:
- ParcelLine costs about **£7,500 a month (around £90,000 a year)** more than SwiftDrop, and about £6,500 a month more than Meridian.
- ParcelLine is the most expensive of the three, even if its whole contact advantage is genuine.
- This leaves out damage-driven one-star reviews, which §2 identifies as a commercial cost.

## 3. The contact reduction is confounded

From 1 May, ParcelLine parcels alone carried the new proactive delivery-day text. That is half the trial. Proactive texts are designed to prevent exactly the "where is my order?" contacts being measured. So "ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts" is not supported.

Splitting ParcelLine's contact rate between April (app only) and May (app plus text) would separate the two effects. Either way, the difference is worth at most about £670 a month, which is small against the damage gap.

## 4. Risks the trial didn't test

- **Peak season.** The trial ran in April and May. ParcelLine's references are mainly from fashion retailers with lighter parcels, while SwiftDrop and Meridian have handled comparable peak volumes. The contract would start in October, just ahead of peak.
- **Heavier parcels.** ParcelLine charges the highest price for 2–10 kg parcels and has the highest damage rate. Breaking damage down by weight band would show whether lamps, mirrors and furniture drive the 0.9%. If they do, the gap will grow during peak and with any shift toward heavier items.
- **The contract term.** A 12-month term limits exposure, but switching carriers has its own costs and risk. It does not offset failing the requirements from day one.

## What holds

These parts of the paper are sound:
- The randomised trial design, with allocation by the warehouse system.
- All of the price and contact arithmetic.
- The integration, collection, tracking, returns and proof-of-delivery comparisons, which are level across all three carriers.
- The point that Meridian's 24-month term is a real consideration.

## Summary

**Settled now:**
- ParcelLine fails the on-time and damage requirements.
- Once damage and loss are costed, ParcelLine is the most expensive option.
- The contact reduction can't be credited to the app.

**Still open, and what would settle each:**

| Question | How to settle it |
|---|---|
| Which of the two compliant carriers to choose | Weigh SwiftDrop (cheapest all-in, 12-month term, damage close to the 0.5% limit) against Meridian (best service, about £1,000 a month more, 24-month term). Check SwiftDrop's damage rate on 2–10 kg parcels. |
| Whether the app or the text cut contacts | Compare April and May contact rates for ParcelLine. |
| Peak-season performance | Ask SwiftDrop and Meridian for peak on-time and damage figures from their reference customers. |

**Recommendation:** award the contract to SwiftDrop on a 12-month term, with the 95% on-time and 0.5% damage requirements written in as contractual service levels. Choose Meridian instead if service quality outweighs about £12,000 a year and the longer term.
